import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Mean percentile rank of the candidates crowded out by taking each candidate, minus 0.5."""
    k = len(values)
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    d = values / np.maximum(weights, 1).astype(float)
    order = np.argsort(d, kind="stable")
    ranks = np.empty(k, dtype=float)
    ranks[order] = np.arange(k, dtype=float)
    r = ranks / max(k - 1, 1)

    # sort candidates by weight ascending
    w_order = np.argsort(weights, kind="stable")
    w_sorted = weights[w_order].astype(float)
    r_sorted = r[w_order]

    # suffix sums / counts of r over the weight-sorted array
    suffix_sum = np.concatenate([np.cumsum(r_sorted[::-1])[::-1], [0.0]])
    suffix_cnt = np.concatenate([np.arange(k, 0, -1, dtype=float), [0.0]])

    # threshold: items with weight > remaining - weights[i] are displaced
    thresh = remaining - weights[i] if False else (remaining - weights.astype(float))
    t = np.searchsorted(w_sorted, thresh, side="right")

    total_sum = suffix_sum[t]
    total_cnt = suffix_cnt[t]

    # remove self if self is in the displaced set (weights[i] > remaining - weights[i])
    self_in = weights.astype(float) > thresh
    total_sum = total_sum - np.where(self_in, r, 0.0)
    total_cnt = total_cnt - np.where(self_in, 1.0, 0.0)

    mean_r = np.where(total_cnt > 0, total_sum / np.maximum(total_cnt, 1.0), 0.5)
    out = mean_r - 0.5
    return np.where(total_cnt > 0, out, 0.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """(v_i + S_i*(remaining - w_i)) / (max(v) + dmax*remaining), S_i = best density among other items fitting the leftover."""
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    weights = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    k = values.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)

    d = values / np.maximum(weights, 1.0)
    dmax = float(np.max(d)) if k > 0 else 0.0

    room = remaining - weights  # >= 0 since each weight <= remaining

    # For each candidate i, best density among j != i with weights[j] <= room_i.
    # Sort items by weight ascending; prefix/suffix maxima of density over that order.
    order = np.argsort(weights, kind="stable")
    w_sorted = weights[order]
    d_sorted = d[order]

    # prefix max over sorted order (inclusive)
    pref = np.maximum.accumulate(d_sorted)
    # suffix max over sorted order (inclusive)
    suff = np.maximum.accumulate(d_sorted[::-1])[::-1]

    # For each candidate i, find count of items with weight <= room_i (in sorted order).
    # idx = number of sorted items with w_sorted <= room_i
    idx = np.searchsorted(w_sorted, room, side="right")  # shape (k,)

    # best over all j with w_sorted[j] < idx, excluding i itself.
    # We need max over prefix [0, idx) minus possibly i.
    # Position of i in sorted order:
    # Since argsort is stable and weights may tie, find each i's sorted position.
    pos = np.empty(k, dtype=np.int64)
    pos[order] = np.arange(k)

    best = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    for i in range(k):
        end = idx[i]
        if end <= 0:
            best[i] = 0.0
            continue
        p = pos[i]
        if p < end:
            # i is inside the prefix; combine prefix before p and suffix from p+1 to end
            left = pref[p - 1] if p > 0 else -np.inf
            right = suff[p + 1] if p + 1 < k else -np.inf
            # right must be restricted to indices < end
            if p + 1 < end:
                right_val = np.max(d_sorted[p + 1:end])
            else:
                right_val = -np.inf
            m = max(left, right_val)
            best[i] = m if np.isfinite(m) else 0.0
        else:
            # i is outside the prefix; best is prefix max up to end
            best[i] = pref[end - 1]

    S = np.maximum(best, 0.0)

    num = values + S * room
    den = np.max(values) + dmax * remaining + 1e-9
    return num / den

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Signed distance of this item's weight from the residual capacity, in units of the typical candidate weight (how many 'typical grains' short of exact fit, or over)."""
    v = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    rem = float(remaining) if remaining > 0 else 1.0
    cap = float(capacity) if capacity > 0 else 1.0
    # typical grain: median candidate weight, robust to outliers
    grain = float(np.median(w)) if w.size > 0 else 1.0
    grain = max(grain, 1.0)
    # signed shortfall: positive = item leaves a gap, negative = item overshoots? here always w<=rem
    short = (rem - w) / grain
    # compress: 0 at exact fit, grows as the leftover is many typical grains
    return np.tanh(short / 3.0) - 0.5

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Density band reward (near-best densities get ~1) times how well the item's weight fits the residual capacity (fill closeness), minus the density shortfall — so among near-tied densities the one that best plugs the remaining room wins."""
    v = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    rem = float(remaining) if remaining > 0 else 1.0
    dens = v / np.maximum(w, 1.0)
    dmax = np.max(dens) if dens.size > 0 else 0.0
    g = (dmax - dens) / max(dmax, 1e-12)
    band = np.exp(-np.square(g / 0.15))
    # fill closeness: reward items whose weight uses a good chunk of the residual room
    fill = np.clip(w / rem, 0.0, 1.0)
    # peak at fill ~ 0.5-1.0, penalty for tiny bites
    fit = fill * (1.0 - 0.5 * fill)
    return band * fit - 0.5 * g
feature.measures: Density band reward (near-best densities get ~1) times how well the item's weight fits the residual capacity (fill closeness), minus the density shortfall — so among near-tied densities the one that best plugs the remaining room wins.

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Opportunity cost of the residual left after taking each candidate: how much value density the leftover space could still buy, relative to the candidate's own density."""
    v = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    k = len(v)
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    rem = float(remaining) if remaining > 0 else 1.0
    dens = v / np.maximum(w, 1.0)
    room_after = rem - w
    # best density among candidates that would still fit in the leftover space
    # (vectorised via sorting: for each candidate, max density with weight <= room_after)
    order = np.argsort(w, kind="stable")
    ws = w[order]
    ds = dens[order]
    # running max of density over ascending weight
    run_max = np.maximum.accumulate(ds)
    idx = np.searchsorted(ws, room_after, side="right") - 1
    best_after = np.where(idx >= 0, run_max[np.clip(idx, 0, k - 1)], 0.0)
    # value the leftover space can buy per unit density: room_after * best_after
    lost_opportunity = room_after * best_after
    # candidate's own value contribution
    own = v
    # ratio: opportunity lost vs value gained (scaled by capacity to bound)
    cap = float(capacity) if capacity > 0 else 1.0
    raw = (own - lost_opportunity) / cap
    return np.tanh(raw / 500.0)

# The problem: 0/1 knapsack, built item by item

There are n items, each with a positive integer value and weight, and one knapsack with a weight capacity. A solution is a set of items whose total weight is at most the capacity; the goal is the largest total value. Each item is taken at most once.

The solution is built one item at a time. One **decision** = choosing the next item to add; the **candidates** are all items not yet taken whose weight still fits in the remaining capacity, in their original index order. The chosen item is added for good (nothing is ever removed) and the build stops when no remaining item fits.

Four training families (Pisinger's classic generators), 100-200 items each, weights in 1-1000, capacity = half the total weight: `uncorrelated` (value uniform in 1-1000, independent of weight), `weakly_correlated` (value within ±100 of the weight, at least 1), `strongly_correlated` (value = weight + 100), `inverse_strongly_correlated` (weight = value + 100). The **gap** of an instance is 1 − value ÷ the optimal value (exact, by dynamic programming), in %.

## A feature

```python
import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """One line: exactly what this measures."""
    ...
    return values   # one number per candidate
```

- `values`: shape (k,), int: the value of every candidate item (the items not yet taken that still fit), in index order.
- `weights`: shape (k,), int: their weights (each ≤ `remaining`).
- `remaining`: int: the capacity still free.
- `capacity`: int: the knapsack's total capacity (it differs between instances: normalise by it).
- `taken`: int: how many items have been added so far.
- Return one finite number per candidate (shape (k,)), or a few columns (shape (k, c)), roughly in [-1, 1].
- Import only `numpy` and `math`. No state between calls, no randomness, don't modify the inputs, no Python loops over candidates when a vectorised form exists (features run thousands of times per evaluation). Guard every division and log.
- Return finite numbers, roughly in [-1, 1] (normalise; the optimiser rescales anyway).

## How the policy works

priority(candidate) = w1 * feature1 + w2 * feature2 + ...; the highest priority wins; on a tie, the first candidate wins. With no features every candidate scores 0, so the first candidate always wins: that is **Code Zero**, the starting point (0% progress). An optimiser fits the weights, including their signs. A new feature is kept only if the policy does better with it than the same refit without it, on training instances *and* on separate validation instances, and the gain isn't already given by the kept features.

## How policies are scored

Per instance, the **gap** is how far the solution is above a reference (lower is better). The score is the mean gap over families. **Progress** is the share of the way from Code Zero (0%) to the best reachable (100%).

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Density band reward (near-best densities get ~1) times how well the item's weight fits the residual capacity (fill closeness), minus the density shortfall — so among near-tied densities the one that best plugs the remaining room wins."""
    v = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    rem = float(remaining) if remaining > 0 else 1.0
    dens = v / np.maximum(w, 1.0)
    dmax = np.max(dens) if dens.size > 0 else 0.0
    g = (dmax - dens) / max(dmax, 1e-12)
    band = np.exp(-np.square(g / 0.15))
    # fill closeness: reward items whose weight uses a good chunk of the residual room
    fill = np.clip(w / rem, 0.0, 1.0)
    # peak at fill ~ 0.5-1.0, penalty for tiny bites
    fit = fill * (1.0 - 0.5 * fill)
    return band * fit - 0.5 * g

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Signed distance of this item's weight from the residual capacity, in units of the typical candidate weight (how many 'typical grains' short of exact fit, or over)."""
    v = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)

    cap = float(capacity) if capacity > 0 else 1.0

    grain = max(grain, 1.0)
    # signed shortfall: positive = item leaves a gap, negative = item overshoots? here always w<=rem

    return np.tanh(short / 3.0) - 0.5

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Opportunity cost of the residual left after taking each candidate: how much value density the leftover space could still buy, relative to the candidate's own density."""
    v = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    w = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    k = len(v)
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    rem = float(remaining) if remaining > 0 else 1.0
    dens = v / np.maximum(w, 1.0)
    room_after = rem - w
    # best density among candidates that would still fit in the leftover space
    # (vectorised via sorting: for each candidate, max density with weight <= room_after)
    order = np.argsort(w, kind="stable")
    ws = w[order]
    ds = dens[order]
    # running max of density over ascending weight
    run_max = np.maximum.accumulate(ds)
    idx = np.searchsorted(ws, room_after, side="right") - 1
    best_after = np.where(idx >= 0, run_max[np.clip(idx, 0, k - 1)], 0.0)
    # value the leftover space can buy per unit density: room_after * best_after
    lost_opportunity = room_after * best_after
    # candidate's own value contribution
    own = v
    # ratio: opportunity lost vs value gained (scaled by capacity to bound)
    cap = float(capacity) if capacity > 0 else 1.0
    raw = (own - lost_opportunity) / cap
    return np.tanh(raw / 500.0)
feature.measures: Opportunity cost of the residual left after taking each candidate: how much value density the leftover space could still buy, relative to the candidate's own density.

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """(d_i - best surviving density after taking i) / (d_i + best + eps), clipped to [-1, 1], with the survivor set restricted to items that still fit *and* are not the candidate itself, computed via a weight-sorted prefix top-2 that excludes the candidate by position."""
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    weights = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    k = values.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)

    d = values / np.maximum(weights, 1.0)
    dmax = np.max(d)
    if not np.isfinite(dmax) or dmax <= 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    room = remaining - weights  # residual capacity after taking each candidate

    # Sort items by weight ascending (stable) and build prefix top-2 of d.
    order = np.argsort(weights, kind="stable")
    w_sorted = weights[order]
    d_sorted = d[order]
    # Position of each original item in the sorted array.
    pos = np.empty(k, dtype=np.int64)
    pos[order] = np.arange(k)

    # Prefix top-1 and top-2 (by value, ties allowed as distinct entries).
    top1 = np.empty(k)
    top2 = np.empty(k)
    m1 = -np.inf
    m2 = -np.inf
    for p in range(k):
        v = d_sorted[p]
        if v > m1:
            m2 = m1
            m1 = v
        elif v > m2:
            m2 = v
        top1[p] = m1
        top2[p] = m2

    # t_i = number of items with weight <= room_i.
    t = np.searchsorted(w_sorted, room, side="right")

    best = np.zeros(k)
    for i in range(k):
        ti = int(t[i])
        if ti <= 0:
            best[i] = 0.0
            continue
        pi = int(pos[i])
        if pi >= ti:
            # Candidate itself is not in the prefix (shouldn't happen since w_i <= room_i,
            # but guard anyway): take the full prefix max.
            best[i] = top1[ti - 1]
            continue
        # Candidate is inside the prefix. Exclude it by position.
        # Max over prefix excluding position pi:
        #   - if pi == ti-1: it's the last entry, so max over [0..ti-2] = top1[ti-2] (or 0 if ti==1)
        #   - else: max(top1[pi-1] over [0..pi-1], top1[ti-1] over [pi+1..ti-1])
        # We only have prefix maxima, not suffix maxima, so handle via top-2 when pi is the
        # unique max; otherwise the prefix max is unaffected by removing a non-max entry.
        m = top1[ti - 1]
        if d[i] < m:
            # Candidate is not the prefix max: removing it changes nothing.
            best[i] = m
        else:
            # Candidate equals the prefix max. If a duplicate of d[i] exists in the prefix,
            # the max survives; otherwise fall back to the second largest.
            s = top2[ti - 1]
            if s == d[i]:
                best[i] = d[i]
            else:
                best[i] = s if np.isfinite(s) else 0.0

    denom = d + best + 1e-9
    out = (d - best) / denom
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

The comparison 'my density minus the best density still available after this pick' is a different object: it depends on which items my weight removes (room_i = remaining - w_i), so a heavy dense item and a light dense twin no longer score alike. It rewards a pick that is strictly ahead of everything it leaves behind, and scores +1 when nothing survives (last-fit), which is exactly the endgame that leaves 42 units unused in uncorrelated.

import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """Mean percentile rank of the candidates crowded out by taking each candidate, minus 0.5."""
    k = len(values)
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    d = values / np.maximum(weights, 1).astype(float)
    order = np.argsort(d, kind="stable")
    ranks = np.empty(k, dtype=float)
    ranks[order] = np.arange(k, dtype=float)
    r = ranks / max(k - 1, 1)

    # sort candidates by weight ascending
    w_order = np.argsort(weights, kind="stable")
    w_sorted = weights[w_order].astype(float)
    r_sorted = r[w_order]

    # suffix sums / counts of r over the weight-sorted array
    suffix_sum = np.concatenate([np.cumsum(r_sorted[::-1])[::-1], [0.0]])
    suffix_cnt = np.concatenate([np.arange(k, 0, -1, dtype=float), [0.0]])

    # threshold: items with weight > remaining - weights[i] are displaced
    thresh = remaining - weights[i] if False else (remaining - weights.astype(float))
    t = np.searchsorted(w_sorted, thresh, side="right")

    total_sum = suffix_sum[t]
    total_cnt = suffix_cnt[t]

    # remove self if self is in the displaced set (weights[i] > remaining - weights[i])
    self_in = weights.astype(float) > thresh
    total_sum = total_sum - np.where(self_in, r, 0.0)
    total_cnt = total_cnt - np.where(self_in, 1.0, 0.0)

    mean_r = np.where(total_cnt > 0, total_sum / np.maximum(total_cnt, 1.0), 0.5)
    out = mean_r - 0.5
    return np.where(total_cnt > 0, out, 0.0)

feature.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(values, weights, remaining, capacity, taken):
    """(v_i + S_i*(remaining - w_i)) / (max(v) + dmax*remaining), S_i = best density among other items fitting the leftover."""
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    weights = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
    k = values.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)

    d = values / np.maximum(weights, 1.0)
    dmax = float(np.max(d)) if k > 0 else 0.0

    room = remaining - weights  # >= 0 since each weight <= remaining

    # For each candidate i, best density among j != i with weights[j] <= room_i.
    # Sort items by weight ascending; prefix/suffix maxima of density over that order.
    order = np.argsort(weights, kind="stable")
    w_sorted = weights[order]
    d_sorted = d[order]

    # prefix max over sorted order (inclusive)
    pref = np.maximum.accumulate(d_sorted)
    # suffix max over sorted order (inclusive)
    suff = np.maximum.accumulate(d_sorted[::-1])[::-1]

    # For each candidate i, find count of items with weight <= room_i (in sorted order).
    # idx = number of sorted items with w_sorted <= room_i
    idx = np.searchsorted(w_sorted, room, side="right")  # shape (k,)

    # best over all j with w_sorted[j] < idx, excluding i itself.
    # We need max over prefix [0, idx) minus possibly i.
    # Position of i in sorted order:
    # Since argsort is stable and weights may tie, find each i's sorted position.
    pos = np.empty(k, dtype=np.int64)
    pos[order] = np.arange(k)

    best = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    for i in range(k):
        end = idx[i]
        if end <= 0:
            best[i] = 0.0
            continue
        p = pos[i]
        if p < end:
            # i is inside the prefix; combine prefix before p and suffix from p+1 to end
            left = pref[p - 1] if p > 0 else -np.inf
            right = suff[p + 1] if p + 1 < k else -np.inf
            # right must be restricted to indices < end
            if p + 1 < end:
                right_val = np.max(d_sorted[p + 1:end])
            else:
                right_val = -np.inf
            m = max(left, right_val)
            best[i] = m if np.isfinite(m) else 0.0
        else:
            # i is outside the prefix; best is prefix max up to end
            best[i] = pref[end - 1]

    S = np.maximum(best, 0.0)

    num = values + S * room
    den = np.max(values) + dmax * remaining + 1e-9
    return num / den

If leftover space is being mispriced, this probe should raise fill/lower unused capacity; if not, it will be flat and tell us the endgame is already handled by f016.

notes.result: not attempted: no feature under it is close to a duplicate or to the kept features (nearest rho < 0.93, R^2 < 0.98)

nodes.title: Relative value rank
nodes.description: Rank by value relative to the max value among candidates (scale-free comparison).

nodes.title: wide find: density_residual_bite
nodes.description: Value density, but scaled by how much of the residual capacity this item would consume.

nodes.title: Slack closing
nodes.description: Prefer candidates whose weight nearly equals the remaining capacity, sharply rewarding exact fits to eliminate leftover slack.

nodes.title: Density gap to next tier
nodes.description: Measure how far a candidate's density exceeds the density of the next-best alternative, rewarding decisive picks over marginal ones.

nodes.title: Weight parity to slack
nodes.description: Score candidates by how close their weight is to remaining capacity modulo typical item weight, targeting near-perfect fills.

notes.result: not attempted: no feature under it is close to a duplicate or to the kept features (nearest rho < 0.93, R^2 < 0.98)

nodes.title: Endgame slack rescue
nodes.description: When remaining capacity is small relative to capacity, switch from density to best-fit weight matching so leftover slack is minimized.

argued.argument: Pairwise residual matching is not a function of density or exact-fit slack; no algebraic identity with kept features holds.

notes.result: not proven: stays at lower priority

nodes.title: Correlation-aware density tilt
nodes.description: Tilt density ranking by the spread of value-minus-weight across candidates, exploiting strong-correlation structure where v-w is constant.

nodes.title: Tightness-conditioned density
nodes.description: Density relative to best, but gated by fill fraction so it only dominates when remaining capacity is scarce.

nodes.title: wide find: displaced_best_density_regret_ratio
nodes.description: Regret of taking this item: the best density lost among items that would no longer fit, relative to this item's own density.

nodes.title: Displaced weight regret
nodes.description: Density relative to best, corrected by the total weight of high-density items that would no longer fit if this item is taken (weight-based, not density-based, regret).

nodes.title: Density gap to runner-up
nodes.description: How far a candidate's density exceeds the second-best density among fitting items, rewarding decisive picks.

nodes.title: Runner-up gap among survivors
nodes.description: Density lead over the best rival that still fits after this pick, so the margin measures competition that survives the decision rather than the full candidate set.

nodes.title: Displaced set regret
nodes.description: Total value (or density mass) of all higher-density items that stop fitting once this item is taken, not only the single best displaced item.

nodes.title: Greedy rollout value
nodes.description: One-step lookahead: the candidate's own value plus the best density still achievable on the space it leaves, value_i + d_after * (remaining - w_i), normalised.
